headline: Mass uprising ends 16 years of Awami League rule in Bangladesh, PM departs
summary: Today marks two years since a historic student-people's mass uprising led to the end of the Awami League government's 16-year rule. The movement saw the departure of the then-Prime Minister and several key figures.
details: Today marks the second anniversary of the historic August 5th, 2024, when a student-people's mass uprising brought an end to the Awami League government's 16-year tenure. The then-Prime Minister and several important individuals left the country amid the widespread movement.

This new chapter in the nation's political history followed a 36-day movement that resulted in over a thousand fatalities. What began as an anti-discrimination student movement, sparked by calls for quota reform, gradually transformed into a mass uprising involving people from all walks of life.

On August 5, 2024, Dhaka was tense from morning, with crowds swelling on the streets as the day progressed, eventually turning into a sea of people. The 'Long March to Dhaka' saw participation not only from students and political activists but also from worried mothers, fathers, members of martyr families, relatives, and countless ordinary citizens.

Amidst this situation, the then-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina eventually left Ganabhaban. News of her departure spread through various media outlets, but with no official announcement, all eyes were on the Army Chief's scheduled address.

The Army Chief confirmed Sheikh Hasina's departure in a televised address to the nation, delivered around 3 PM. Following this announcement, people across Dhaka and other parts of the country erupted in joyous celebrations, with the student-people's sea reaching Ganabhaban in a victory procession.
caption:

headline_marked: [[Six Naya Dhara leaders taken into custody]] after Press Club clash, DMCH standoff
headline: Six Naya Dhara leaders taken into custody after Press Club clash, DMCH standoff
summary: The custody followed a violent clash with Rashtra Sanglap Forum members near Jatiya Press Club and a three-hour standoff at Dhaka Medical College Hospital, disrupting emergency services.
details: Police took six leaders and activists of Naya Dhara Bangladesh into custody on Tuesday night. This action followed a clash with members of the Rashtra Sanglap Forum near the Jatiya Press Club and a subsequent three-hour standoff at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).

The six individuals, including Naya Dhara Chairman Momin Mehedi and Senior Vice-Chairman Shanta Farzana, were escorted out of the hospital’s emergency department under police protection around 11:10pm. They were then taken away in a police vehicle.

Inspector Mainul Islam Khan Pulok of Shahbagh Police Station confirmed they were in police custody, though a decision on formal arrest had not yet been made. The initial clash erupted during a Naya Dhara protest against an alleged assault on Shanta Farzana.

Several people from both sides, including Shanta and Rashtra Sanglap Forum Member Secretary ANM Ayas, sustained injuries and were taken to DMCH for treatment. Afterwards, members of the Rashtra Sanglap Forum gathered outside the hospital, confining Naya Dhara leaders inside the emergency department.

This situation caused disorder within the emergency department, disrupting medical services for approximately one and a half hours and creating fear among patients and their attendants, according to DMCH police. Police intervened to manage the tense situation.

The two organizations provided conflicting accounts of how the clash began. Rashtra Sanglap Forum leaders alleged that Shanta made offensive remarks about July fighters and the BNP, leading to an attack by Naya Dhara activists when they protested.

Conversely, Naya Dhara Chairman Momin Mehedi claimed that ANM Ayas arrived at their program with a group and attacked his party’s leaders and activists. He also alleged that the attackers confiscated phones from journalists present at the scene.
caption:
